messages.subject: Re: Bad probability tables?
messages.body_plain:
hi,

i'm new to deal, and don't know if you're still looking for a 
solution to this but i think i may have found one(for discrete 
variables anyway).  in the document found at:

http://www.jstatsoft.org/v08/i20/updates/deal.pdf on page 6 it talks 
about finding the discrete part (of the joint prior) by dividing
(yourjointprior$jointalpha) by (sum of yourjointprior$jointalpha)

by applying the same logic to this problem: if you look at the nodes 
of your network: nodes(network), and divide the individual 
conditional posterior values for each node by the sum of the 
conditional posterior values for that node then this will give 
values that sum to 1 (as far as my testing shows anyway!)

if there's an easier way this newbie would love to know!

regards, lisa.

> 0.04862798 )     % :c

0.05251499
> )     % :t
>      normal (  0.000149588+0.5002583 * seq+0.4945506 * TF,  
0.04970229 )
> % :c+t

0.4172805 )
> % :c-t
>      normal (  -0.007082273+0.006636849 * seq+0.002752811 * TF, 
> 0.04286846 )     % :0
>      );
> }
> 
> 
> I focus on the node labeled "gene" (discrete, 5 possible states), 
which
> should be dependent on the node labeled "cond" (discrete, 3 
possible
> states). This conditional relationship is also mentioned in 
the .net
> file ("potential ( gene | cond )"). Yet the table does not look 
very
> convincing, as neither rows (as i would expect) nor columns sum up 
to
> 1.0. By looking further into this in R, i found the following 
(nw.best
> is the network i actually exported using savenet()):
> 
> > nw.best$nodes$gene$prob
>                  c         t        c+t        c-t          0
> Lin     0.4992636 0.4876923 0.61131611 0.07815631 0.07977528
> Neutral 0.3843888 0.4123077 0.31365314 0.28657315 0.29887640
> Stab    0.1163476 0.1000000 0.07503075 0.63527054 0.62134831
> 
> So there i have colsums 1.0. But to correctly reflect the 
relationship
> (also shown as arrow from "cond" to "gene" in the plot of nw.best) 
there
> should be rowsums, if i am not mistaken. Any ideas where i am 
wrong or
> if this indeed is a wrong calculation of deal?
> The exporting method obviously swaps the table around (columns 
become
> rows, but there are only 3...). I already know, that the .net 
format
> allows for continuous specification of such tables, but 
nevertheless, as
> i understand bayesian networks, there should be 5 consecutive 
entries
> summing up to 1.0, to reflect the actual dependency.
> 
> thanks
> 
> markus

messages.subject: getnetwork function
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I read in the manual for the deal package that the function
getnetwork() returns a network family of all tried networks when
applied to the result of heuristic(). But when I tried it, it only
returned one network even when I tried the built-in "rats" example.
How can I obtain all the networks heuristic() calculated and their
scores to draw and compare them? And is the network which I obtained
by using getnetwork() the best network?

Thank you for your help!
Marit

messages.subject: Re: getnetwork function
messages.body_plain:
Dear Marit

You might have read an outdated version of the manual. (Try 
http://cran.r-project.org/doc/packages/deal.pdf). Or better, the help-
page for 'heuristic' - in the examples you will see the 'hisc2' 
object and how to display it using gettable and makenw.

The behaviour of 'getnetwork' was changed to cope with one of the 
memory problems in 'deal'

best,

Claus
